expectations.text: Root cause identified is the missing email normalization at write time, NOT merely 'search uses == comparison'.
expectations.evidence: Root cause is one level deeper than the comparison: 'Email identity is undefined and unowned. The store exposes raw string equality, does not enforce uniqueness, and every flow mistakes string equality for same user.' Why 3 names the write path: 'Signup stores the email exactly as typed, and nothing in the write or read path canonicalises it' citing app/signup.py:15 and app/db.py:26. The recommended fix adds a canonical key computed on insert and enforced for uniqueness, i.e. write-time normalisation at the store boundary, not a search-only patch.

The root cause is that... The recommended fix moves... That closes the search bug...'). The skill's own fix.md section 8 says 'Headline. One sentence'. Section first sentences otherwise pass: each states its claim directly (e.g. section 5 'Every flow that looks a user up by email shares the defect', section 6.5 'Confirmed.'), no teasers.

notes: Strong run on substance: the chain is accurate against the fixture, the fix.patch applies cleanly and passes all 7 tests when I replayed it, the fixture copy was restored byte-identical to the pristine original, and the data sibling (pre-existing duplicate rows becoming unreachable) is a genuine insight no assertion rewards. Two gaps: the assumptions list (skill step 5.5) was skipped entirely, and the headline spans four sentences where the skill demands one. On the eval itself: assertion 6's 'normalization at write time' is narrower than the best answer (identity owned at the store boundary on both read and write; write-only normalisation would leave existing rows broken), so consider rewording to accept either. Assertion 13's one-sentence headline fights the 25-word lint cap, so a run that passes both will be terse to the point of lossy; decide whether that is the intended bar. Nothing checks that the agent left the pristine fixture untouched and restored the copy, which this run did well and a careless run would not.
